newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan coffee bonds launch seen in two months.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan coffee bonds launch seen in two months.

text.p: A top Nicaraguan coffee grower said the government is enthusiastic about a proposed $40 million to $50 million coffee bond deal and plan to issue them within two months.

"There have been major advances in the coffee bonds and I think the bonds can be working in less than two months," Eduardo Rizo, executive president of the Nicaraguan Union of Coffee Growers (Unicafe), told Reuters Tuesday.
Rizo said Unicafe presented the plan for the asset-backed security bonds to Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman, who was "very enthusiastic" about the idea.
"He is very much in agreement with the bonds. The only item we still have to work out with the government is how we are going to use the funds," he said.

Rizo said the government wants the money raised through the bond issue to be used to build Nicaragua's coffee-growing infrastructure while Unicafe wants the money to be used for infrastructure and financing coffee growers.
He said Aleman, himself a coffee grower who lives on his coffee farm outside Managua, was interested in using the funds to improve the bad state of roads in coffee-growing regions.
"We have to reach an agreement on this issue, but basically we have everything ready to go," he said.
Rizo said the five-year bonds will be called Coffee Certificates (Certicafe) and will be also backed by the government to generate investor confidence.
